verdict.rationale: Browserbase is a browser-agent platform, so adaptive crawling is a fair question to ask of it, but the evidence pack never documents a crawling mode that stops automatically once enough information has been gathered to answer a query. The nearby features are different capabilities: web search (docs-2), URL-to-markdown fetch (docs-3), goal-driven agents (docs-16), and pauseWhen (docs-23), which pauses a run for human input rather than ending a crawl on sufficiency.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can rely on adaptive crawling that automatically stops once enough information has been gathered to answer my query
